background:
1 Timothy: The Letter, Its World and Your Notes

Study notes · dates are approximate and scholars vary

At a glance

1 Timothy is a letter from Paul to his younger co-worker Timothy, whom he had left in Ephesus to correct false teaching and set the church in order. Traditionally it dates from about AD 62–64, after Paul's release from his first Roman imprisonment.

QuestionTraditional viewNotes
AuthorPaul (1:1)With 2 Timothy and Titus, one of the “Pastoral Letters.” Many modern scholars think a follower of Paul wrote them later; the traditional view holds they are Paul's.
DateAbout AD 62–64Acts does not record this period; Paul seems to have been released, traveled again, and later re-arrested.
Written fromMacedonia (1:3)Paul had urged Timothy to remain at Ephesus while he went on to Macedonia.
RecipientTimothy, “my true child in faith” (1:2)From Lystra, son of a Jewish believing mother and a Greek father (Acts 16:1); Paul's companion for about fifteen years.
The problemTeachers obsessed with “fables and endless genealogies” (1:4)They also forbade marriage and certain foods (4:3) and treated godliness as a way to get rich (6:5).
Purpose“That thou mayest know how men ought to behave themselves in the house of God” (3:15)Instructions on prayer, leaders, widows, elders, slaves and the rich.

The letter centers on a short confession of faith: Christ “was manifested in the flesh… Received up in glory” (3:16).

Dates are approximate. The Pastoral Letters fit best after the end of Acts, during Paul's last years.

The time map

The shaded band marks the traditional date, AD 62–64, between Paul's release and Nero's persecution.

Rome and society in the early 60s

1 Timothy addresses a church in one of Rome's richest cities, where wealth, status and family law shaped daily life.

  • Nero's harsher years. After AD 62 Nero's chief advisers were gone and his reign grew more cruel. Paul urges prayers “for kings and all that are in high place” so that believers may live peaceful lives (2:1–2).
  • Fashion and wealth. Portraits of wealthy Roman women show elaborate braided hairstyles, gold and pearls. Paul urges women to adorn themselves with good works instead (2:9–10).
  • Widows. Augustus' marriage laws pressured young widows to remarry. The church supported genuinely needy widows and urged families to care for their own (5:3–16).
  • Slaves. Believing slaves were to honor their masters, even believing masters, so that God's name would not be slandered (6:1–2).
  • The rich. Wealthy patrons expected honor for their gifts. Paul tells the rich not to be proud or trust in riches, but to be generous (6:17–19).
  • “Savior.” Emperors were hailed as saviors; 1 Timothy calls God “our Saviour” six times.

Paul wants a church whose orderly, generous, godly life will commend the gospel to outsiders (3:7; 5:14; 6:1).

Ephesus

Ephesus, capital of Asia and Paul's base for three years (Acts 19), was the setting for Timothy's work.

  • The temple of Artemis. One of the Seven Wonders, with 127 columns. Paul calls the church “the pillar and ground of the truth” (3:15).
  • A great church. Ephesus had several house churches with elders, whom Paul had warned that false teachers would arise from among them (Acts 20:29–30).
  • Magic and myths. Ephesus was known for magic and speculation; false teachers dealt in “fables and endless genealogies” (1:4).
  • Hymenaeus and Alexander. Named as having shipwrecked their faith (1:20). An Alexander also appears in the Ephesus riot (Acts 19:33) and in 2 Tim 4:14.
  • Timothy's youth. Timothy was perhaps in his early thirties, young for a leader in a culture that honored age (4:12).
  • Asceticism. Some taught that marriage and certain foods were wrong (4:3); Paul answers that everything God created is good if received with thanksgiving.

Around the world in the early 60s

1 Timothy was written as Nero's reign was darkening.

RegionWhat was happening
BritainBoudica's revolt (AD 60–61). The queen of the Iceni burned London, Colchester and St Albans before being crushed.
RomeNero's early good years ended about AD 62. The Great Fire of AD 64 was followed by the first persecution of Christians.
JudeaTension grew; James the Lord's brother was killed in AD 62. The Jewish revolt broke out in AD 66.
Armenia and ParthiaA compromise peace in AD 63; Nero crowned the Parthian prince Tiridates king of Armenia in Rome in AD 66.
ItalyAn earthquake damaged Pompeii and Herculaneum in AD 62, seventeen years before Vesuvius buried them.
ChinaThe Eastern Han dynasty under Emperor Ming; silk reached Rome along the trade routes.
IndiaThe Kushan Empire was forming in the northwest; tradition says Thomas preached in India.
The AmericasTeotihuacan was growing; the Moche and Nazca cultures flourished in Peru.

How the setting shapes the study

1 Timothy's instructions make more sense against life in Roman Ephesus.

PassageConnection to the times
1 Tim 1:4“Fables and endless genealogies”: speculative stories, perhaps built on Old Testament family lines.
1 Tim 1:17“The King eternal, immortal, invisible”: unlike mortal emperors.
1 Tim 2:1–2Prayer for rulers, under Nero, so believers could live quietly.
1 Tim 2:9Roman portraits show elaborate braided hair, gold and pearls among wealthy women.
1 Tim 3:15The temple of Artemis was famous for its columns; the church is the pillar of truth.
1 Tim 5:3–16Roman law pressured young widows to remarry; older widows often had no support.
1 Tim 5:23Water was often unsafe; a little wine was a common remedy.
1 Tim 6:1–2Many believers were slaves; some masters were believers too.
1 Tim 6:10In a wealthy trading city, “the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.”

In a city devoted to Artemis and to wealth, Paul points to the “one God, one mediator also between God and men, himself man, Christ Jesus” (2:5).

Maps: then and now

Ephesus lay on the western coast of Asia (modern Türkiye); Macedonia was across the Aegean, a few days' sail away.

Today Ephesus is one of the best-preserved Roman cities in the Mediterranean, near Selçuk in Türkiye.

items.text: Warning Against False Teachers
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus according to the commandment of God our Saviour, and Christ Jesus our hope;
unto Timothy, my true child in faith: Grace, mercy, peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
As I exhorted thee to tarry at Ephesus, when I was going into Macedonia, that thou mightest charge certain men not to teach a different doctrine,
neither to give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questionings, rather than a dispensation of God which is in faith; so do I now.
But the end of the charge is love out of a pure heart and a good conscience and faith unfeigned:
from which things some having swerved have turned aside unto vain talking;
desiring to be teachers of the law, though they understand neither what they say, nor whereof they confidently affirm.
But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully,

as knowing this, that law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and unruly, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,
for fornicators, for abusers of themselves with men, for menstealers, for liars, for false swearers, and if there be any other thing contrary to the sound doctrine;
according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.
Christ Came to Save Sinners
I thank him that enabled me, even Christ Jesus our Lord, for that he counted me faithful, appointing me to his service;
though I was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: howbeit I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief;
and the grace of our Lord abounded exceedingly with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
Faithful is the saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief:
howbeit for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me as chief might Jesus Christ show forth all his longsuffering, for an ensample of them that should thereafter believe on him unto eternal life.
Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory for ever and ever. Amen.
This charge I commit unto thee, my child Timothy, according to the prophecies which led the way to thee, that by them thou mayest war the good warfare;
holding faith and a good conscience; which some having thrust from them made shipwreck concerning the faith:
of whom is Hymenæus and Alexander; whom I delivered unto Satan, that they might be taught not to blaspheme.

summary.title: CHAPTER 1 IN SUMMARY
paras: Paul reminds Timothy why he left him in Ephesus: to command certain people not to teach different doctrine or devote themselves to myths and endless genealogies, which promote speculation instead of God's work. The goal of Paul's instruction is “love out of a pure heart and a good conscience and faith unfeigned.” These teachers want to be teachers of the Law without understanding it; the Law is good when used to expose sin.

Paul thanks Christ for appointing him to service, though he was once a blasphemer and persecutor, because he received mercy. “Faithful is the saying… that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.” He was shown mercy as an example of Christ's patience. He charges Timothy to fight the good fight, holding faith and a good conscience, which some, like Hymenaeus and Alexander, have rejected and shipwrecked their faith.

questions.label: OBSERVE
questions.text: How does Paul describe his own past and the mercy he received in verses 12–16, and why does he call himself the chief of sinners?

questions.label: THEN
questions.text: In Ephesus, a center of learning and religious speculation, why would fables and endless genealogies (v. 4) have been a real danger to the church?

questions.label: NOW
questions.text: Paul says the goal of instruction is love from a pure heart, good conscience and sincere faith (v. 5); how might that goal reshape your learning?

items.text: Prayer for All People
I exhort therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, thanksgivings, be made for all men;
for kings and all that are in high place; that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and gravity.
This is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour;
who would have all men to be saved, and come to the knowledge of the truth.
For there is one God, one mediator also between God and men, himself man, Christ Jesus,
who gave himself a ransom for all; the testimony to be borne in its own times;
whereunto I was appointed a preacher and an apostle (I speak the truth, I lie not), a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
Men and Women in Worship
I desire therefore that the men pray in every place, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and disputing.
In like manner, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefastness and sobriety; not with braided hair, and gold or pearls or costly raiment;
but (which becometh women professing godliness) through good works.
Let a woman learn in quietness with all subjection.
But I permit not a woman to teach, nor to have dominion over a man, but to be in quietness.
For Adam was first formed, then Eve;
and Adam was not beguiled, but the woman being beguiled hath fallen into transgression:
but she shall be saved through her child-bearing, if they continue in faith and love and sanctification with sobriety.

summary.title: CHAPTER 2 IN SUMMARY
paras: First of all, Paul urges prayers and thanksgiving for all people, for kings and all in authority, so that believers may lead a quiet and peaceful life. This pleases God our Savior, “who would have all men to be saved, and come to the knowledge of the truth. For there is one God, one mediator also between God and men, himself man, Christ Jesus, who gave himself a ransom for all.”

Men everywhere should pray, lifting holy hands without anger or quarreling. Women should adorn themselves modestly, not with braided hair, gold, pearls or costly clothing, but with good works. Paul then gives instructions about women learning quietly and not teaching or exercising authority over men, grounding them in the creation account, and says women will be saved through childbearing if they continue in faith, love and holiness.

questions.label: OBSERVE
questions.text: For whom does Paul urge prayers in verses 1–2, and what reasons does he give about God's desire and the one mediator (vv. 3–6)?

questions.label: THEN
questions.text: Why would praying for kings and all in authority (v. 2) matter for a small church living under Roman rule and suspected by its neighbors?

questions.label: NOW
questions.text: Christians read verses 9–15 in different ways; how can your group study these verses carefully while treating differing views with charity and respect?

items.text: Qualifications for Overseers
Faithful is the saying, If a man seeketh the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.
The bishop therefore must be without reproach, the husband of one wife, temperate, sober-minded, orderly, given to hospitality, apt to teach;
no brawler, no striker; but gentle, not contentious, no lover of money;
one that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity;
(but if a man knoweth not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?)
not a novice, lest being puffed up he fall into the condemnation of the devil.
Moreover he must have good testimony from them that are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
Qualifications for Deacons
Deacons in like manner must be grave, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre;
holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
And let these also first be proved; then let them serve as deacons, if they be blameless.
Women in like manner must be grave, not slanderers, temperate, faithful in all things.
Let deacons be husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.
For they that have served well as deacons gain to themselves a good standing, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.
The Mystery of Godliness
These things write I unto thee, hoping to come unto thee shortly;
but if I tarry long, that thou mayest know how men ought to behave themselves in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.

And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness; He who was manifested in the flesh, Justified in the spirit, Seen of angels, Preached among the nations, Believed on in the world, Received up in glory.

summary.title: CHAPTER 3 IN SUMMARY
paras: If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a good work. An overseer must be above reproach, faithful in marriage, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach, not a drunkard or violent, not quarrelsome or a lover of money; he must manage his household well, not be a new convert, and have a good reputation with outsiders.

Deacons too must be dignified, honest, not greedy, holding the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience, tested first, and managing their households well; the women likewise must be dignified and faithful. Paul writes so that Timothy will know how to behave in God's household, “the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.” Great is the mystery of godliness: Christ “who was manifested in the flesh, Justified in the spirit, Seen of angels, Preached among the nations, Believed on in the world, Received up in glory.”

questions.text: What qualities for overseers and deacons are listed in verses 1–13, and which relate to character rather than ability?

questions.label: THEN
questions.text: Why would a leader's reputation with outsiders (v. 7) have mattered so much for a church in Ephesus watched closely by its pagan neighbors?

questions.label: NOW
questions.text: Verse 16 summarizes the mystery of godliness; which line of this early confession most strengthens your faith or invites deeper reflection?

items.text: Some Will Depart from the Faith
But the Spirit saith expressly, that in later times some shall fall away from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons,
through the hypocrisy of men that speak lies, branded in their own conscience as with a hot iron;
forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God created to be received with thanksgiving by them that believe and know the truth.
For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected, if it be received with thanksgiving:
for it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer.
A Good Servant of Christ Jesus
If thou put the brethren in mind of these things, thou shalt be a good minister of Christ Jesus, nourished in the words of the faith, and of the good doctrine which thou hast followed until now:
but refuse profane and old wives’ fables. And exercise thyself unto godliness:
for bodily exercise is profitable for a little; but godliness is profitable for all things, having promise of the life which now is, and of that which is to come.
Faithful is the saying, and worthy of all acceptation.
For to this end we labor and strive, because we have our hope set on the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of them that believe.
These things command and teach.
Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an ensample to them that believe, in word, in manner of life, in love, in faith, in purity.
Till I come, give heed to reading, to exhortation, to teaching.
Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.
Be diligent in these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy progress may be manifest unto all.
Take heed to thyself, and to thy teaching. Continue in these things; for in doing this thou shalt save both thyself and them that hear thee.

summary.title: CHAPTER 4 IN SUMMARY
paras: The Spirit says that in later times some will depart from the faith, following deceitful spirits and teachings of demons, forbidding marriage and requiring abstinence from foods God created to be received with thanksgiving. “For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected, if it be received with thanksgiving.”

Timothy will be a good servant of Christ by teaching these things. He should reject silly myths and train himself for godliness, which is profitable for all things, holding promise for this life and the life to come. “Let no man despise thy youth”; instead Timothy should be an example in speech, conduct, love, faith and purity, devote himself to public reading of Scripture, exhortation and teaching, and not neglect his gift. He must watch his life and doctrine closely.

items.text: Instructions About Widows
Rebuke not an elder, but exhort him as a father; the younger men as brethren:
the elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, in all purity.
Honor widows that are widows indeed.
But if any widow hath children or grandchildren, let them learn first to show piety towards their own family, and to requite their parents: for this is acceptable in the sight of God.
Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, hath her hope set on God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day.
But she that giveth herself to pleasure is dead while she liveth.
These things also command, that they may be without reproach.
But if any provideth not for his own, and specially his own household, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an unbeliever.
Let none be enrolled as a widow under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man,

well reported of for good works; if she hath brought up children, if she hath used hospitality to strangers, if she hath washed the saints’ feet, if she hath relieved the afflicted, if she hath diligently followed every good work.
But younger widows refuse: for when they have waxed wanton against Christ, they desire to marry;
having condemnation, because they have rejected their first pledge.
And withal they learn also to be idle, going about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.
I desire therefore that the younger widows marry, bear children, rule the household, give no occasion to the adversary for reviling:
for already some are turned aside after Satan.
If any woman that believeth hath widows, let her relieve them, and let not the church be burdened; that it may relieve them that are widows indeed.
Honoring Elders
Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in the word and in teaching.
For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn. And, The laborer is worthy of his hire.
Against an elder receive not an accusation, except at the mouth of two or three witnesses.
Them that sin reprove in the sight of all, that the rest also may be in fear.
I charge thee in the sight of God, and Christ Jesus, and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without prejudice, doing nothing by partiality.
Lay hands hastily on no man, neither be partaker of other men’s sins: keep thyself pure.
Be no longer a drinker of water, but use a little wine for thy stomach’s sake and thine often infirmities.
Some men’s sins are evident, going before unto judgment; and some men also they follow after.
In like manner also there are good works that are evident; and such as are otherwise cannot be hid.

summary.title: CHAPTER 5 IN SUMMARY
paras: Paul tells Timothy to treat older men as fathers, younger men as brothers, older women as mothers and younger women as sisters, in all purity. The church should honor widows who are truly alone and devoted to prayer, while children and grandchildren must care for their own family members; anyone who does not provide for his household has denied the faith. Older widows of good character may be enrolled, but younger widows should marry and manage homes, to give no occasion for reproach. Elders who rule well, especially those who labor in preaching and teaching, are worthy of double honor, for “The laborer is worthy of his hire.” Accusations against an elder need two or three witnesses, and those who persist in sin should be rebuked publicly. Timothy must act without partiality, not lay hands on anyone hastily, and keep himself pure, using a little wine for his stomach's sake. Some sins are obvious, others appear later, and good works likewise cannot remain hidden.

questions.label: OBSERVE
questions.text: How does Paul tell Timothy to treat older and younger men and women in verses 1–2, and what family image governs it?

questions.label: THEN
questions.text: Without pensions or social welfare in the Roman world, why was it important to distinguish widows supported by family from widows the church should care for (vv. 3–16)?

questions.label: NOW
questions.text: Paul stresses caring for one's own household (v. 8); who in your family or church family needs practical care you could help provide?

items.text: Slaves and Masters
Let as many as are servants under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honor, that the name of God and the doctrine be not blasphemed.

And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren; but let them serve them the rather, because they that partake of the benefit are believing and beloved. These things teach and exhort.
False Teaching and True Contentment
If any man teacheth a different doctrine, and consenteth not to sound words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness;
he is puffed up, knowing nothing, but doting about questionings and disputes of words, whereof cometh envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings,
wranglings of men corrupted in mind and bereft of the truth, supposing that godliness is a way of gain.
But godliness with contentment is great gain:
for we brought nothing into the world, for neither can we carry anything out;
but having food and covering we shall be therewith content.
But they that are minded to be rich fall into a temptation and a snare and many foolish and hurtful lusts, such as drown men in destruction and perdition.
For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil: which some reaching after have been led astray from the faith, and have pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
Fight the Good Fight of Faith
But thou, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness.
Fight the good fight of the faith, lay hold on the life eternal, whereunto thou wast called, and didst confess the good confession in the sight of many witnesses.
I charge thee in the sight of God, who giveth life to all things, and of Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed the good confession;
that thou keep the commandment, without spot, without reproach, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ:
which in its own times he shall show, who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;
who only hath immortality, dwelling in light unapproachable; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honor and power eternal. Amen.
Instructions for the Rich
Charge them that are rich in this present world, that they be not highminded, nor have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches, but on God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy;
that they do good, that they be rich in good works, that they be ready to distribute, willing to communicate;
laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on the life which is life indeed.
O Timothy, guard that which is committed unto thee, turning away from the profane babblings and oppositions of the knowledge which is falsely so called;
which some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with you.

summary.title: CHAPTER 6 IN SUMMARY
paras: Slaves should honor their masters so that God's name and teaching are not slandered, and those with believing masters should serve them all the better. Anyone who teaches otherwise is puffed up, craving controversy and supposing godliness is a means of gain. “But godliness with contentment is great gain”; having food and clothing, we should be content, for “the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.”

Timothy, as a man of God, must flee these things and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience and gentleness, fighting the good fight of the faith and keeping the commandment until Christ appears, at the time appointed by “the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords; who only hath immortality.” The rich must not be haughty or trust in uncertain riches but in God; they should do good, be rich in good works, and be generous, laying a good foundation for the future. Timothy must guard what has been entrusted to him.

questions.label: THEN

questions.label: NOW

wrap.title: 1 Timothy In Summary
paras: 1 Timothy is a letter from an experienced missionary to a younger colleague facing a hard assignment. Paul had left Timothy in Ephesus to stop false teachers who were spreading speculative myths, forbidding marriage and certain foods, and treating religion as a way to get rich. The letter equips Timothy to lead the church well.

At its heart is the gospel itself. “Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief” (1:15). God our Savior wants all people to be saved, and there is one mediator between God and men, Christ Jesus, who gave Himself as a ransom for all (2:4–6). The church exists to hold up this truth, as “the pillar and ground of the truth” (3:15). Because the church is God's household, Paul gives practical instructions for its order: prayer for all people including rulers, conduct in worship, qualifications for overseers and deacons, care for widows, honor and discipline for elders, and the attitudes of slaves and masters. The qualities required of leaders are mostly about character: self-control, faithfulness, hospitality, gentleness and freedom from the love of money.

Paul also gives Timothy personal counsel. He should not let anyone despise his youth, but set an example; devote himself to Scripture and teaching; train himself in godliness; and flee the love of money, pursuing righteousness, faith, love and gentleness. Godliness with contentment is great gain, and the rich should be generous rather than proud.

The message in one line: the church, as God's household and the pillar of His truth, must guard the gospel of Christ who came to save sinners, and show it in sound teaching, godly leaders and lives of love, contentment and generosity.
